archive_02_001.speaker: narrator
archive_02_001.text: The school trustee arrived at breakfast carrying two parcels wrapped in the same cloth. One contained the retained account copy; the other contained flat cakes for Sun Nian. The trustee put the cakes down first, and Dai's mouth tightened until Sun laughed. She had once taught this woman to write numbers in columns, she explained, and had accepted worse bribes in the shape of plums. The cakes belonged to breakfast. The document would wait until the appointed table had been cleared.

archive_02_002.speaker: narrator
archive_02_002.text: Luo carried away the breakfast bowls himself. He set four chairs around the table: Sun's, Dai's, the trustee's and his own. Yue had been assigned to make the agreed school extract, but she was not one of Sun's four listeners. She took her unused paper to the adjoining workroom. Through the closed door came the scrape of Sun's walking stick, followed by silence. Yue had expected a request for extra help. Instead, the meeting began without asking her to become its invisible fifth participant.

archive_02_003.speaker: narrator
archive_02_003.text: Tan brought a frame whose cloth sling held the damaged register at a shallow angle. The original remained in the workroom while the trustee's certified copy went inside. Yue watched Tan compare the treatment diagram with the actual tear. At the bottom of the page, two little arches resembled a pair of eyebrows raised in astonishment. Tan said a child had once practised drawing faces in the margin. They would retain the marks. Someone's impatience with accounts had survived longer than the missing total.

archive_02_004.speaker: tan_ke
archive_02_004.text: My first master would have called those eyebrows damage. She could repair a fold beautifully, but she thought every book should appear innocent of having been read. I used to agree with her. Then I found a volume she had treated thirty years earlier, and its blank margin was where a pupil had named an uncredited teacher. I cannot tell you whether she meant to erase him. I can tell you how careful a person becomes after discovering that care has removed a name.

archive_02_005.speaker: narrator
archive_02_005.text: The workroom window faced the school path. Children passed in pairs, carrying wooden writing boards under their coats. One boy had chalked a cloud on his sleeve and was trying to protect it from the drizzle. His companion held a spare board over the cloud rather than over the boy's head. Yue's amusement faded when the school bell failed to sound. A woman on the path called the pupils forward with a spoon and a bowl. Inside the meeting room, someone began to speak more loudly.

archive_02_006.speaker: narrator
archive_02_006.text: A first request came through the door after half an hour. Luo asked for the already permitted extract showing the advance, its date and the surviving repayment note. Yue brought only that sheet to the threshold. She saw the trustee's hands flat beside her copy and Sun looking toward the window. The copy supplied the missing sum: eighteen copper for boards, chalk and a stove repair. The original's surviving line recorded sixteen returned, leaving two. No one had yet agreed what the remaining two represented.

archive_02_007.speaker: narrator
archive_02_007.text: Yue went back to the supported register. The margin beneath the repayment entry contained a small upright stroke that resembled an abbreviated name. Dai had earlier catalogued it as uncertain writing. A junior clerk wanted to call it a confirmation mark, because the figures would then reconcile with the trustee's copy. Tan moved the lamp rather than the page and let the shadows change. The upright stroke resolved into the tail of the pupil's cartoon. The clerk blushed, and Yue revised nothing except the working note.

archive_02_008.speaker: lin_yue
archive_02_008.text: It would have been an agreeable mistake. The account would balance, and we could all feel that an old debt had become tidy. But that boy's eyebrow has done more than entertain us. It has stopped us from making a witness out of an ink stroke. I am writing that the mark remains a drawing under the present light. If another examination changes that description, it will need to explain the change, rather than inherit our wish to finish the arithmetic.

archive_02_009.speaker: narrator
archive_02_009.text: Inside, the trustee argued that her predecessor had carried the two copper forward as a personal debt owed by the teacher. Sun remembered the teacher repairing the stove with a part taken from his own kitchen. She remembered the old trustee promising to deduct its price. She did not remember seeing the deduction made. The meeting's writer separated those statements before reading them back. Sun interrupted at the word promised. She had heard the old trustee say he would ask the committee; that was all.

archive_02_010.speaker: narrator
archive_02_010.text: Dai emerged to fetch the committee minute book. She opened its request list to an uncompleted entry from the same winter, then paused. The book's second volume was among the five boxes moved on the first day. She had not yet allowed it to be unwrapped because the cord was moulded against the cover. Tan examined it before agreeing to a supported opening. A small decision at breakfast had become an hour's delay. From the school path, the spoon struck the bowl again.

archive_02_011.speaker: narrator
archive_02_011.text: The trustee came out during the delay to ask Yue whether children could borrow a table at the archive for the afternoon. Their stove flue had split overnight, and rain was entering through the hole where the old pipe had stood. Yue could offer no room herself. She took the request to Luo, who was already hurrying toward the door. Dai stopped him only long enough to distinguish a supervised lesson from public admission to the closed shelves. He returned with the receiving-room key and a relieved expression.

archive_02_012.speaker: narrator
archive_02_012.text: Sun remained at the table while the other three briefly considered the lesson arrangements. She tapped her stick on the floor and asked them to finish hearing the witness they already had before recruiting the children as an argument. The trustee looked abashed. Luo sat down again. Dai instructed the clerk to record the interruption and its reason, not the words traded over the doorway. When the door closed, Yue felt the workroom recover its proper size. She had something useful to do without being summoned into the dispute.

archive_02_013.speaker: narrator
archive_02_013.text: The receiving room filled with wet coats after noon. The pupils counted themselves aloud so that the teacher could compare voices with the morning list. One child announced that the archive smelled like his grandmother's sleeping cupboard. The cook supplied warm water and refused to let the bowls become drums. Yue carried a screen across the room so the pupils' chalk dust would stay clear of the conservation table. The screen was painted with mountains so improbable that the children immediately began correcting them.

archive_02_014.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_02_014.text: I commissioned that screen twelve years ago. The painter charged by the mountain, which may explain the geography. Your lesson can use the plain side if you prefer. Please leave the legs where they are; the floor beneath the middle panel has already been checked, and the other boards are being repaired. If anyone wants to improve my mountains, begin on your own slate. I have waited twelve years to learn whether the blue lump is a hill or an unfortunate sheep.

archive_02_015.speaker: narrator
archive_02_015.text: The joke travelled through the archive faster than the lesson noise. Even Dai smiled when a child asked whether the sheep required a separate catalogue entry. She then returned to the meeting with the second committee volume. The retained copy had been checked against this book four years earlier, but its certificate referred only to the advance entry. It had never certified the later committee decision. Dai laid two slips side by side. The comparison date that had reassured everyone now explained why something important could still be absent.

archive_02_016.speaker: narrator
archive_02_016.text: The later minutes approved the replacement stove part at two copper. A subsequent line authorised deducting that sum from the teacher's materials advance. The signature was clear. Beneath it, an empty box should have contained a posting reference. The old trustee had agreed the deduction but never carried it into the debt column. Sun closed her eye for a moment. She had spent years wondering whether she remembered a promise invented to make an exhausted winter kinder. The proof was narrower than that feeling, and considerably stronger.

archive_02_017.speaker: narrator
archive_02_017.text: The current trustee's account copy was accurate to the page it reproduced. Her inherited debt list was accurate to a column that had not been updated. Neither fact made the debt collectible after the missing approval was found. Luo wanted to tell the teacher's family immediately. Dai wanted the clerk to finish a dated correction first, so the family would receive a usable answer. For once the difference between them was an interval measured in minutes. They agreed on the order without raising their voices.

archive_02_018.speaker: sun_nian
archive_02_018.text: I am glad the book says what it says. I am not glad enough to remember the teacher's entire life correctly. He sometimes arrived late. He could be sharp with boys who hid their slates, and he was kind to a girl whose shoes leaked. You have an account to correct, not a saint to build. If you mention my testimony in the correction, use the stove conversation I agreed to give you. The other things I have just said are why I need my tea.

archive_02_019.speaker: narrator
archive_02_019.text: The clerk crossed out the active claim in the current school ledger with a single line and entered the committee reference beside it. Dai watched without demanding a copied image of the teacher's face or an account of his family. Luo prepared the message. The trustee insisted on signing it herself. She had collected neither of the disputed copper, but she had sent two reminders to a surviving daughter. The correction would identify the earlier reminders and withdraw them, giving the daughter something she could show without retelling her grief.

archive_02_020.speaker: narrator
archive_02_020.text: There was a snag in the corrected amount. A late fee of one copper had already been entered against the daughter when she did not answer the second reminder. That fee belonged to the current trustee's term, not the old posting error. The trustee acknowledged it without asking the older mistake to absorb her own. She removed the fee in a separate entry. The school still needed a working stove, and its accounts were now three copper poorer on paper. They were also three copper closer to the truth.

archive_02_021.speaker: narrator
archive_02_021.text: He Xi appeared at the outside window with a crate of borrowed stools. He had completed his assigned delivery and stopped to receive the clerk's return receipt. The sight of Sun through the glass made him lift his hand, but he did not enter. The children wanted the crate turned into a boat. He laid it flat on the receiving-room floor and pretended to inspect their imaginary harbour. Yue saw that he looked younger among the children than he had with the carrying straps cutting into his shoulders.

archive_02_022.speaker: narrator
archive_02_022.text: When the lesson ended, its teacher counted the pupils again and led them toward the hostel kitchen for their agreed meal. The receiving room retained eleven damp footprints and a drawing of Luo's blue sheep on a slate left behind. Luo asked Yue to preserve the slate until the owner returned. Dai, passing the doorway, asked whether the sheep had a named owner or an uncertain attribution. The joke startled Luo into laughter. He had spent so many weeks arguing with her that he looked almost suspicious of the sound.

archive_02_023.speaker: narrator
archive_02_023.text: The meeting concluded before sunset. Sun accepted the agreed travel payment and took the trustee's cake parcel home in her own cloth bag. She refused a public commendation for correcting the account. A commendation would probably arrive with another request attached, she said, and she was saving her strength for a neighbour's birthday. The clerk read her permitted statement back once more. She removed an adjective calling the teacher generous. She had described a stove part and a committee request; generosity was a judgment someone else could defend.

archive_02_024.speaker: narrator
archive_02_024.text: Yue helped Tan settle the minute book on its padded support. The cord had left a greenish stain but had not transferred growth onto the opened leaves. The result would need another inspection after drying; the first safe opening did not complete treatment. Tan washed her hands slowly, keeping the water away from the apron. She had brought the stained cord out in a separate tray. Instead of congratulating herself over the recovered deduction, she wrote down the tool that had slipped while lifting the knot.

archive_02_025.speaker: tan_ke
archive_02_025.text: The tool did no damage this time. That is precisely why I ought to record the slip while I still remember it. Tomorrow I may use the same angle on a more brittle cover and discover that confidence is a poor material for supporting paper. Today the best page was in an ordinary minute book, under a cord nobody admired. If I start imagining myself as the person who finds answers, I will become careless with the places where an answer fails to appear.

archive_02_026.speaker: narrator
archive_02_026.text: The carpenter returned from the school with a sketch of the broken flue. Rain could be kept out cheaply for a few days, but the cracked pipe needed replacement before the stove could be lit. The school roof fund had money restricted to slate work, and the general account would cover only half the pipe. The trustee wanted permission to use the slate allocation for the pipe immediately. Dai could not grant it. The restriction came from an endowment lodged at the archive, not from the archive's own budget.

archive_02_027.speaker: narrator
archive_02_027.text: Luo went to the catalogue cabinet with the current school charter number. Yue expected another large book and instead received a thin bundle with a red cotton tie. It contained the founder's endowment terms, two amendments and a printed notice summarising them. The first amendment allowed temporary classrooms elsewhere when the school building became unsafe. The second concerned the use of the adjoining orchard. The summary mentioned both but printed only a short phrase about repairs. That phrase had become the trustee's account heading, carrying less detail than the original authority.

archive_02_028.speaker: narrator
archive_02_028.text: The founder's endowment required the school to maintain a dry teaching room and a working winter stove. It named roofs and flues together. The printed notice's shorter phrase had become, in successive ledgers, a roof-only allocation. For a moment Luo looked ready to declare a second complete victory. Dai held up the second amendment. It reserved a later gift specifically for slates. Two funds had been folded into one heading after a treasurer retired. Separating them would require the actual balances, not simply a better reading of the charter.

archive_02_029.speaker: narrator
archive_02_029.text: The school's carpenter waited without pretending the problem was his account to solve. He could fit the new pipe when the correct money was available, and he could close the opening tonight with a removable cover. The trustee authorised that cover from the unrestricted emergency amount already in her account. Luo paid the archive's agreed stool hire from its visitor fund. Yue wrote the return time beside the receipt. The day ended with a debt corrected and children housed, but tomorrow's lesson still required a warm room.

archive_02_030.speaker: narrator
archive_02_030.text: In the kitchen, He was arguing with a child who insisted that courier work must be easy because all a courier needed was to remember where houses stood. He took a spare bowl and turned it over on the table. That was one hill. A folded cloth was another, and the cook's hand immediately reclaimed it. He then used his own cap. The child sent a bean across the valley between the hills. He tilted the table slightly with one finger and the bean vanished beneath a stool.

archive_02_031.speaker: he_xi
archive_02_031.text: That is the season when everyone says the path is still there. They mean the houses are still there and the people are still waiting. The path has gone somewhere under the mud, and you must decide whether finding it will cost more than the letter pays. I like my work. I even like some of the hills. But if you become a courier, charge for the road you must actually walk, not the line your customer draws between two comfortable chairs.

archive_02_032.speaker: narrator
archive_02_032.text: Yue retrieved the bean and handed it back to the child. She had arrived with a road in her own mind that seemed nearly as simple: come north, perform useful work, leave with wages and a clearer sense of training. Already the archive had given her a room whose door she should not enter and a debt whose correction depended on a cartoon eyebrow. She found these details less discouraging than the grand work she had imagined. They required attention she could offer without pretending attention would be enough for everything.

archive_02_033.speaker: narrator
archive_02_033.text: Dai ate last, after the teacher's corrected claim message had left with an ordinary district courier. She kept her spectacles on during the meal until the cook told her they made the stew nervous. When she removed them, Yue noticed how much more tired her face became. Dai had known the unpaid teacher. She had catalogued his donated books after his death and accepted the trustee's debt list as separate school business. No one had asked her to compare the two. She said this without attempting to make omission look like neutrality.

archive_02_034.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_02_034.text: I can explain why I did not open the school accounts. I had a roof that leaked and deposits whose owners expected me to protect them. Those explanations are true, but they are not the entire answer. I liked him, and the debt offended the memory I kept. I may have avoided the papers because I thought I would find an ordinary failure behind someone I preferred to admire. We corrected an entry today. I will need longer to decide what I owe the people who waited for us.

archive_02_035.speaker: narrator
archive_02_035.text: Luo began to reassure her and then stopped. The cook asked whether either of them intended to leave enough hot water for the dishes. Dai stood, took a stack of bowls and carried them to the basin. Luo followed with the pot. Their conversation changed from the dead teacher to whether the basin shelf could bear a full pot. Yue was grateful for the interruption. A person could have more work to do after an admission and still wash a bowl without turning it into a ceremony.

archive_02_036.speaker: narrator
archive_02_036.text: The following morning was Yue's fourth paid calendar day. Her first six-day working stretch would end after the sixth, leaving the seventh free under the appointment. She marked the date on her own page while the trustee's ledger balances were brought up from the school. Luo asked for her help comparing their references. The work lay within her copying assignment, but it would take the hours reserved for box labels. Tan agreed to the swap because the boxes were safely supported and could wait one more morning.

archive_02_037.speaker: narrator
archive_02_037.text: Three columns emerged from the school's books: the original maintenance endowment, the later slate gift and unrestricted fees. Years of totals had been carried forward correctly; years of headings had not. The maintenance fund retained enough to replace the flue and patch the teaching-room plaster, after separating the slate amount. The trustee sat back as if someone had moved the hill under her house. Money she had imagined inaccessible was available, but she would need a public correction of the fund descriptions before using it.

archive_02_038.speaker: narrator
archive_02_038.text: A school committee meeting could be called in two days, with the quorum named in its existing rules. Emergency cover would last that long if the weather did not worsen. The teacher agreed to continue classes at the archive until the flue was installed and inspected. The archive's receiving room could spare mornings but was booked for a petition session on the sixth afternoon. Luo wrote the school hours beside the other use instead of assuming one useful purpose had displaced another. The schedule looked increasingly like a field planted in narrow rows.

archive_02_039.speaker: narrator
archive_02_039.text: The trustee asked whether her corrected account would embarrass the school in front of its donors. Dai answered that concealing a usable stove fund while borrowing a classroom would be more difficult to defend. That was a sharp answer, and the trustee's face hardened. Luo intervened before the argument became a contest in shame. The public notice could state that two funds had been merged under an inaccurate heading, list their current balances and name the permitted repair. It could also state that classes had continued safely while the account was corrected.

archive_02_040.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_02_040.text: You do not owe the donors a story in which none of us makes a mistake. You owe them the uses their gifts authorised. That means the slates remain slates and the stove can become a stove again. If a donor dislikes seeing the old heading corrected, I will sit through that conversation with you. I cannot sit through it in your place, because the school account is yours to answer for. I can bring the copies we have compared and describe how we reached them.

archive_02_041.speaker: narrator
archive_02_041.text: Yue copied the notice draft, leaving the committee decision date blank. A child came back for the sheep slate and recognised his own chalk marks instantly. He was offended that Luo had called his drawing a sheep. It was clearly the archive's rain gutter. Luo examined it gravely and apologised to the gutter. The boy then asked why adults needed so many papers to decide whether a pipe should keep water out. Yue answered that different people had supplied the money for different things. The boy asked why they had not written that more clearly.

archive_02_042.speaker: narrator
archive_02_042.text: The plain question stayed with her during the afternoon's box labelling. She chose words a person could understand while cold and impatient: opened under support, awaiting treatment, restricted owner packet. Tan corrected one label that said repaired when it meant surface dirt removed. Beyond the workroom door, Dai was drafting instructions for someone who might need to take over her duties unexpectedly. The day had frightened her into recognising how much authority remained lodged in her memory of familiar cases. She had no intention of dying, she told Yue, but that was a poor filing method.

archive_02_043.speaker: narrator
archive_02_043.text: He came for his wages at the end of the unloading contract. The steward counted the completed deliveries and paid the agreed sum without subtracting the stools he had borrowed for the archive's lesson. Those belonged to a separate hire authorised by Luo. He checked the coins, tied the pouch and then asked about the fourth-afternoon petition session. His own packet was still in the guarded cabinet. He had arrived expecting a quick acknowledgement and discovered that proper receipt was only the first step toward being heard.

archive_02_044.speaker: narrator
archive_02_044.text: Dai took his petition number from the entry list. The session could confirm admissibility and identify which deposited instruments needed notice to their other parties. It would not settle inheritance that afternoon. He looked disappointed but did not argue with a promise she had not made. Yue had no reason to hear the packet yet, and moved to the far table when He asked Dai a personal question. Through the window she saw a gust press rain sideways across the yard. The temporary school cover held.

archive_02_045.speaker: narrator
archive_02_045.text: The next morning brought sunshine sharp enough to reveal every stain on the receiving-room floor. Sun returned for her walking stick cap, which had rolled beneath a chair during the meeting. She carried no notebook and had accepted no further witness appointment. Luo tried to describe the stove fund discovery. She listened politely until he began connecting it to the founder's family, then told him she was going to market. The fact that she knew an old teacher did not make every old account her afternoon's responsibility.

archive_02_046.speaker: narrator
archive_02_046.text: Yue walked as far as the lower gate with her during a scheduled break. Sun wanted an elbow on the steps, not a hand on her bag, and made the distinction with an impatient click of her tongue. At the gate, she stopped to watch two boys chase a loose chicken away from the washing line. Her face softened when one boy abandoned the chase to retrieve the other boy's fallen shoe. Yue asked whether she had known their parents. Sun said yes, but she was enjoying knowing the boys.

archive_02_047.speaker: sun_nian
archive_02_047.text: Old people become archives if everyone insists on it. You ask who I remember, and I am obliged to produce dead mothers, dead teachers, winters worth making notes about. Sometimes I would like to be the woman who saw a boy carry another boy's shoe this morning. That is not a complaint about your question, child. It is advice about the next one. Begin with what is happening while we are both here. We can visit the dead later, if we have agreed on the journey.

archive_02_048.speaker: narrator
archive_02_048.text: Back inside, Yue found Luo measuring the receiving-room wall for a new notice board. The old notices had overlapped until their bottom corners concealed one another's dates. He wanted school hours, petition hours and temporary roof closures visible at the same time. Dai arrived with a shorter version of the instructions he had written. To Yue's surprise, the two stewards argued over which version required less prior knowledge. Luo's used simpler words but relied on an unlabelled map. Dai's named the rooms but used three abbreviations no visitor would understand.

archive_02_049.speaker: narrator
archive_02_049.text: They gave both versions to the cook, who removed the abbreviations, demanded a doorway arrow and said the phrase authorised attendance made her expect a tax collector. The resulting notice required one more sheet than Luo had budgeted. He paid for the sheet from the visitor stationery amount and pasted it below the map. It was neither Dai's draft nor his. For the rest of the day each quoted the cook's chosen wording as if it had always been the obvious phrase, to her visible irritation.

archive_02_050.speaker: narrator
archive_02_050.text: The school committee assembled on the sixth day of Yue's appointment. Its members sat among the children’s corrected mountains while the teacher held lessons outside in the mild weather. The account comparison was read aloud, questions answered and the two fund headings restored. The members approved payment for the flue from the maintenance endowment. A donor's nephew objected that his uncle's slate gift was being raided. Dai showed him the separate balance, and the nephew then asked to inspect the copied authority rather than continue arguing with a rumour.

archive_02_051.speaker: narrator
archive_02_051.text: The carpenter took a dated work order and went down to prepare the pipe. The teaching room would reopen only after the fitting and a safe stove test. No one pressed him to light a cracked installation for the sake of a committee photograph. The teacher proposed a public thank-you to the archive for its room. Luo accepted it on behalf of the staff who had moved screens, washed bowls and adjusted other appointments. He named the cook first. She was too busy serving lunch to hear him.

archive_02_052.speaker: narrator
archive_02_052.text: He stood at the edge of the yard that afternoon, waiting for the school clerk to finish with Dai. His mother had sent a fresh cloth for his patched carrying straps and a note asking him not to quarrel during the petition session. He read the note twice before folding it away. Yue, passing with the workroom list, saw how tightly his fingers held the cloth. She asked whether he wanted water. He accepted, and they sat on opposite ends of the garden bench without discussing the packet.

archive_02_053.speaker: he_xi
archive_02_053.text: My mother thinks a quiet petition is more likely to be heard. She may be right. She has worked with people who mistake an angry voice for a request they are free to dismiss. But I am afraid that if I am very quiet, I will help them think nothing has cost us much. I do not know the right volume for this afternoon. I know my father will not come, and she will sit beside me if I ask her. That is already more than last year.

archive_02_054.speaker: narrator
archive_02_054.text: Yue told him she had no tested volume for a family argument. She could say that Dai had corrected an account she once preferred not to open, and that Luo had sat through a donor's questions after promising the trustee he would. Neither observation guaranteed the petition's outcome. He nodded and drank the water as if thirsty for it at last. Across the yard, the donor's nephew helped stack the borrowed stools. He had remained after reading the separate balance, apparently unwilling to leave his uncle represented only by an objection.

archive_02_055.speaker: narrator
archive_02_055.text: The admission session began at the stated hour. He chose to admit Yue as the paid copying assistant for the fields he would submit, along with his mother, Dai and Luo. Tan remained available to examine physical condition without joining the family discussion. The guarded packet contained a retained copy of an inheritance deed and the receipt for its earlier deposit. An original deed belonging to the same matter had been lodged by another party years before. Dai brought out its catalogue description first, so nobody confused possession of a copy with possession of the instrument it represented.

archive_02_056.speaker: narrator
archive_02_056.text: The founder of the school endowment had also owned a small orchard and a house beside its lower gate. He's grandmother had worked there and, according to the retained copy, received a life tenancy in the house with a later right passing to her descendants who maintained the school path. The lodged original was catalogued as a different version. Its summary mentioned the grandmother but did not describe the later right. He's father had moved away after being told the tenancy ended at her death. He and his mother had stayed in rented rooms nearby.

archive_02_057.speaker: narrator
archive_02_057.text: Dai did not read the other party's entire deed into the room merely because He had offered his own. The deposit terms permitted comparison of the relevant inheritance clauses after notice to the current orchard trustees. Those trustees had received notice earlier in the week and appointed one member to attend the next session. Today's work established which fields needed comparison and why. Yue copied the grandmother's name, the house description and the stated maintenance condition from He's admitted sheet. Her hands became very still as the school's path appeared in a private family claim.

archive_02_058.speaker: narrator
archive_02_058.text: Luo said the public endowment instruments could be consulted under their own access terms. Dai nodded, but reminded him that the house deed and the school gift were distinct instruments even if signed by the same person. They put the three document numbers on separate cards. The simple arrangement made He stare. Until then, he had described the matter as the founder's will, as if one lost page might answer every question. There were at least three writings, two relevant dates and people whose interests did not line up neatly with either version.

archive_02_059.speaker: dai_shuren
archive_02_059.text: A difference between copies deserves investigation. It is not yet proof that someone altered the original, and an original may itself contain an error that later lawful work corrected. We will compare dates, endorsements and custody before drawing the legal question. I can promise to show you where our catalogue has compressed something it should have kept distinct. I cannot promise the orchard or the house. If you leave angry today, I would prefer you be angry at that honest answer rather than at a gift I had no authority to offer.

archive_02_060.speaker: narrator
archive_02_060.text: He asked whether the archive had taken money to hide the later clause. The accusation changed the room's temperature more quickly than the rain outside. His mother put a hand on his wrist, but Dai answered before she could withdraw it for him. The archive charged deposits and comparison work according to its published rates. It had recorded no payment for suppressing a clause. That did not prove the whole institution incapable of misconduct. It meant the accusation needed evidence more specific than the fact that He had waited too long.

archive_02_061.speaker: narrator
archive_02_061.text: Yue saw Luo prepare to speak and then decide against defending Dai personally. Instead, he turned the public rates toward He and offered the deposit account entries that the orchard matter's terms allowed them to disclose. A fee paid by the trustees seven years earlier had purchased a new catalogue summary after rebinding. The summary was the one that omitted the later right. He leaned forward. Dai read the instruction attached to the fee: shorten the descriptions to fit the new cabinet cards. It named no alteration of the deed.

archive_02_062.speaker: narrator
archive_02_062.text: The omission in a summary might have been innocent and still have helped exclude a family from its home. Dai acknowledged that before He could say it. She asked the clerk to attach a correction-pending flag to the catalogue card, preserving the old wording as a dated record rather than scraping it clean. That was work the archive could begin now. Ownership of the house would require the comparison and a competent hearing. He looked at the flagged card and seemed to find its modest red edge both inadequate and impossible to dismiss.

archive_02_063.speaker: narrator
archive_02_063.text: His mother spoke for the first time about the path. Every spring she had cleared its drain with three neighbours. They had regarded it as ordinary school work, not performance of an inherited condition. One neighbour had died; another had moved away; the third now sat on the orchard committee. If the retained deed's words mattered, those actions might matter too. She had kept no account because no one had paid her. The fact was painfully common. He asked whether the absence of receipts meant the work would disappear.

archive_02_064.speaker: lin_yue
archive_02_064.text: It means we should not pretend a receipt exists. It does not decide that the work never happened. A witness can describe what she saw, and a school record may name a cleared drain without explaining its family significance. We can identify those sources without making you remember them all tonight. If someone asks you for exact dates you do not have, say so. A year remembered by the flood or a child's first lesson may give us a lead to check, rather than a date to manufacture.

archive_02_065.speaker: narrator
archive_02_065.text: The copying session ended with a comparison appointment three days later, allowing the orchard representative to attend and Dai to check the deed's condition. He received a copy of the questions accepted for review. He had expected to leave with a house key or a rejection. Leaving with three numbers, an appointment and a corrected catalogue flag felt less final than either. In the yard he shook his head once, hard, as if clearing rain from his ears. His mother adjusted the new cloth under his carrying strap without asking him to be grateful.

archive_02_066.speaker: narrator
archive_02_066.text: Yue spent her seventh day off walking above the archive rather than helping with the petition. The path was open, the weather mild, and she returned before evening under the receiving house's visitor guidance. She watched a stream meet another stream and become muddy for several yards. A clear joining did not mean the waters had agreed. Below, the school's new flue stood wrapped beside the carpenter's bench. The orchard beyond it looked ordinary: crooked trees, windfalls and a boy throwing rotten fruit at a fence post.

archive_02_067.speaker: narrator
archive_02_067.text: From that height, the archive's roof appeared as a patchwork of slates rather than an emergency of separate buckets. The carpenter's survey had marked more damage than the first cover could address. Dai's ordinary repair reserve would fund the open joints but not replace the whole failed beam. The archive's governing council had a seasonal grant application pending. Luo had begun to fear that the school's petition and the house claim would make the council wary of spending money on a place now producing so many uncomfortable questions.

archive_02_068.speaker: narrator
archive_02_068.text: When Yue returned from her walk, he was waiting in the yard with a letter already addressed to the council. He asked her to read the plain description of the roof work during her next paid morning. She reminded him that tomorrow would be the eighth day. He smiled ruefully and put the letter away. The evening was hers. They spoke instead about the screen painter and the best way to cook bruised apples. He had lost a daughter in infancy, he said after a silence, and sometimes found children's absurdity easier to bear than their gratitude.

archive_02_069.speaker: narrator
archive_02_069.text: Yue did not ask him to turn the loss into an explanation of every choice he made. He said only that the school lesson had surprised him with pleasure and that he resented Dai for making him wait outside a room when he wanted to be useful. He also understood why Sun had closed the door. Understanding had not removed the resentment. Yue found that admission more encouraging than the finished argument she might have expected. Luo could know a boundary was right and still need time to stop pushing against it.

archive_02_070.speaker: narrator
archive_02_070.text: At supper Dai announced the school flue had been fitted and would be tested the following morning. Until the test passed, classes would remain in the receiving room. The cook demanded the borrowed kettle back as soon as they moved. He had bought a small apple with part of his wages and cut it into four uneven pieces. He offered one to Yue, one to his mother and one to the child who had invented the bean road. The fourth he ate without making it the smallest.

archive_02_071.speaker: narrator
archive_02_071.text: The archive settled after supper into the sound of bowls draining and rainwater falling beyond the windows. Yue entered her seventh day as paid rest, not as a useful extra shift. In the room downstairs, Dai laid the inheritance cards beside the roof application and shut both covers. A corrected school debt had revealed a usable stove fund; the fund had led them toward a house and a path whose meanings were disputed. No recovered sum could answer the next question. For that, people would have to return and sit together again.
